concept: Classical exponential-action projection differs from quantum Krylov diagonalization
summary: Classical Krylov approximation replaces a matrix exponential action by a smaller projected exponential.
limitations: Convergence depends on the operator, time, starting vector, subspace, and numerical precision; no gap-only bound is claimed.
OpenQEvo constructs a dense propagator from independent basis-state actions; it does not expose sparse or hardware execution.
implications: For the dense krylov reference, sweep krylov_dim and compare against exact evolution where feasible.
Check both approximation error and unitarity of the assembled propagator.

evidence.note: Abstract: classical projected matrix-exponential action and error-estimation scope; OpenQEvo API limits are engineering context.
